passages.text: Therefore, with many forms of worship having passed through the world, we—the good merchants—are here bringing you the form of worship handed down to us from our ancestors and preserved, like a pearl, displaying it and placing it before your judgment and at your disposal. Choose what seems good to you. If, then, you choose what is ours, you will not only be able to escape demons and the sufferings caused by demons, but, as you yourselves put them to flight and are implored by them, you will also enjoy the good things that will exist forever.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πολλῶν οὖν ἐν βίῳ παρελθουσῶν θρησκειῶν
lexical_decisions.chosen: Therefore, with many forms of worship having passed through the world
lexical_decisions.rationale: “Therefore” explicitly represents the inferential οὖν. The genitive absolute is rendered circumstantially; it could also be understood concessively, “Therefore, although many forms of worship have passed through the world.” The phrase ἐν βίῳ may mean “in life” or, contextually, “in the world.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πάρεσμεν φέροντες ὑμῖν (οἱ ἀγαθοὶ ἔμποροι) ἐκ προγόνων ἡμῖν παραδοθείσης καὶ φυλαχθείσης θρησκείας ὥσπερ μαργαρίτην
lexical_decisions.chosen: we—the good merchants—are here bringing you the form of worship handed down to us from our ancestors and preserved, like a pearl
lexical_decisions.rationale: The presentation by the speakers is retained before the description of the inherited worship, following the supplied clause order. The genitive θρησκείας is represented idiomatically as what is brought and compared to a pearl; a more formally genitival interpretation is “bringing you, like a pearl, something from or of the worship handed down to us.”
The nominative phrase is appositional to the implied subject of πάρεσμεν and continues the pearl-merchant image.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐπὶ τῇ ὑμετέρᾳ κρίσει καὶ ἐξουσίᾳ τιθέντες
lexical_decisions.chosen: placing it before your judgment and at your disposal
lexical_decisions.rationale: κρίσις denotes judgment or evaluation, while ἐξουσία can denote authority, freedom of action, or power of disposal. The rendering preserves both the evaluation and the hearers’ freedom to choose.

lexical_decisions.chosen: Choose what seems good to you
lexical_decisions.rationale: The substantivized participle denotes what appears good or suitable to the hearers without asserting that their choice is objectively correct.
The neuter plural leaves the referent broad enough to include the speakers’ teaching, worship, and practices.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: αὐτοὶ αὐτὰ φυγαδεύοντες καὶ ἱκετευόμενοι ὑπ’ αὐτῶν
lexical_decisions.chosen: as you yourselves put them to flight and are implored by them
lexical_decisions.rationale: The neuter αὐτά may refer to the sufferings or may collect both the demons and the demonic sufferings just mentioned. The genitive plural αὐτῶν is formally compatible with every gender, so its morphology does not identify its referent; although reference to the sufferings or the preceding collection is grammatically possible, the act of imploring contextually favors the demons as the agents. The English pronouns retain the contextual reference without introducing a gender distinction absent from the Greek form.
